title: Choose the look for Ithaca's App Store screenshots
question: New hand. The roll assigned The One-Sheet. Keep it, take my pick or an alternate, or re-roll again (safer or bolder steers it). Expand a card to see its first iPhone slide full size.

options.label: The One-Sheet
options.lineage: Theatrical one-sheets (27×41 movie posters) and their condensed billing blocks
options.thesis: Each slide is a movie poster for what it sells: the device as key art, the headline as the title, a billing block crediting what Ithaca plays.
options.viewport: A small tagline at the top, the iPhone as key art with the film's art bleeding around it, the headline as the title treatment, the billing block at the foot.
options.risk: A poster of a poster can bury the app; it holds only while the device is the key art, not a prop.

raised.raise: One shelf line: every slide's device stands on the same baseline, so the six line up in the store.
One central axis: tagline, title, device and billing block mirrored on it.
Title at full poster scale against tiny tracked billing; nothing at middle size.
A thin progress line under the device marks where you stopped, the only lit mark besides the screen.

options.label: After Dark
options.lineage: Night photography of real rooms lit only by a screen, as in Apple's own product films
options.thesis: Each slide is a real room after dark, lit only by Ithaca on the screen: the living-room TV, an iPad in bed, an iPhone on the train.
materials: screen glow as the only light
options.viewport: A dark living room with the TV glowing on the wall, the headline in the dark above, the iPhone large in the foreground showing Home.
options.risk: Familiar: Apple's and every streaming service's lifestyle language; needs a generated photo per slide.

options.label: The Prospectus
options.lineage: Late-modern corporate prospectus: a bone-white plate and one rendered ribbon of colour
options.thesis: Almost all white; every bit of colour spent on one ribbon of projector light running from the screen, the dark device alone in the light.
options.viewport: Headline left in two weights, its second line violet; a teal-to-violet ribbon unfurling from the iPhone's screen across the right bleed; the dark iPhone alone below.
options.case: The restraint reads Apple-grade and the device owns the slide; a prospectus says nothing about movies.
options.risk: Can read as a fintech or SaaS ad.

options.label: The Spot-Colour Issue
options.lineage: Mid-century magazine identity programs: one spot colour per issue, a mark hidden on every cover
options.thesis: Each slide is a magazine cover in one spot colour, with Ithaca's mark hidden somewhere in it for patient eyes.
options.viewport: Masthead across the top, the headline with an oversized initial in the left column, the iPhone in the right column bleeding off the foot, the mark hidden in a poster.
options.case: Gives the six slides a collectible issue-by-issue rhythm film lovers notice; the magazine conceit costs some clarity.
options.risk: Editorial costume, and its lineage is Playboy's art direction.

options.label: Brine Calendar
options.thesis: Slides as labelled jars on a shelf.
options.viewport: Jars on a shelf line around the device.
options.case: Fermentation says nothing about film or Plex.
options.kept: One shelf line: every device on the same baseline.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.viewport: A garden axis leading to the device.
options.case: Palace gardens are a costume for a media player.
options.kept: One central axis for every slide.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.lineage: Experiential studio sites with full-screen shaders
options.thesis: A living colour field with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: A colour field with the device floating in it.
options.case: Loses the device to the effect; reads as an agency site.
options.kept: One oversized word against tiny labels.

options.label: Step Row
options.thesis: Sixteen lit keys with a chase light.
options.viewport: A step row under the device.
options.case: A rhythm machine isn't the living room.
options.kept: A light that always shows where now is.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark gradient, a bold centred headline, the device below: what most players ship, done cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and one line on a dark gradient, the iPhone centred below.
canonCard.risk: It is the look of Dusk for Plex's own listing, the app Ithaca descends from.
